newsitem.title: UK: REDLAND LEADS SECTOR HIGHER ON STG OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: REDLAND LEADS SECTOR HIGHER ON STG OUTLOOK.

text.p: Shares in UK building materials group Redland Plc resumed their rebound on Monday, leading a sector rally, amid growing perceptions that UK interest rates and sterling have seen their peaks, dealers said.
By 1131 GMT, Redland shares climbed 8p to 314-1/2, a five-week high.
Elsewhere, shares in RMC Group Plc gained 8-1/2p to 11.13-1/2 stg, while shares in Wolseley Plc firmed 4p to 492-1/2.
"The sector is in vogue at the moment, given the interest rate and currency outlook," said one dealer.

The belief that the Bank of England's last move to tighten credit last week probably was the last put a cap on sterling, which in turn, has boosted the sector as well as shares in other companies with high exposure to foreign exchange rates.
Benign producer price figures released earlier today reinforced the perception that rates probably won't be raised again in the near-term, dealers said.
"The main thing is that the performance of these stocks has been dismal. They're oversold and people were looking for a bit of a bounce," another dealer said.
Redland shares, for instance, fell 23 percent from the beginning of the year to July 31, when they bottomed at 283-1/2p, while leading UK blue chips climbed to historic highs.
